done_state: A zero-dependency read-side library implementing ARCHITECTURE.md section 7's exact consumer contract: resolve current, read index, validate schema_version, validate age, longest path-component match on roots (never picking a candidate on ambiguous), and reading a project detail shard under the SAME resolved generation. Every one of the five named failure modes (pointer missing, pointer dangling, index corrupt, shard corrupt, whole root removed) plus a sixth this component adds (schema_version mismatch) returns a reason and no data -- none raise, matching section 4's stated guarantee.

criteria.statement: Each of the five failure modes named in ARCHITECTURE.md section 7 (pointer missing, pointer dangling, index corrupt, shard corrupt, whole root removed) returns a result object carrying a reason and no data -- none raise an exception out of the public read function.
criteria.verification: atlas/hookclient/tests/test_failure_modes.py: five separate fixtures, one per failure mode, each asserting read_index() returns ok=False with a reason string naming that specific mode, and never raises.

criteria.statement: Reading a valid, fresh snapshot returns the parsed index content and a correctly-computed staleness (age_seconds, is_stale) derived from generated_at and max_age_seconds, not a bare file mtime -- matching section 6's stated design ('cursors... so a reading hook can compute its own staleness instead of trusting a bare file mtime').
criteria.verification: atlas/hookclient/tests/test_freshness.py: a fixture with generated_at set to a known offset from an injectable 'now', asserts age_seconds and is_stale are computed correctly both under and over max_age_seconds.

criteria.statement: Staleness is reported, not enforced -- read_index() returns the data AND is_stale=True for an aged-out snapshot; the caller decides fail-open policy, matching section 5's design that hookclient itself does not decide what a hook does about staleness.
criteria.verification: atlas/hookclient/tests/test_freshness.py: asserts a stale fixture's read_index() result has ok=True (data present) with is_stale=True, not ok=False -- staleness alone is not a failure mode.

criteria.statement: A schema_version in the index that does not match this client's expected version is treated as a failure mode (reason returned, no data), not silently accepted or silently coerced.
criteria.verification: atlas/hookclient/tests/test_failure_modes.py: a fixture index.json with schema_version='atlas-snapshot-1' (an old/wrong version) asserts read_index() returns ok=False naming a schema_version mismatch.

criteria.statement: resolve_project(cwd, index) reproduces section 7's exact consumer contract: longest path-component match against index['roots'], returning unique (one prefix)/ambiguous (the full candidate list, never picking one)/unregistered (proceed as if ATLAS absent) -- reusing atlas.resolve.matcher's own matching function rather than a second, potentially-drifting implementation.
criteria.verification: atlas/hookclient/tests/test_project_resolution.py: fixtures covering unique, ambiguous (the real FORE/AREM shared-root shape), and unregistered cwds against a real index['roots'] map, asserting the returned resolution and candidate list match atlas.resolve.matcher.resolve_cwd's own output on the same input.

criteria.statement: read_project(cwd_or_prefix, index_result) reads the shard from the SAME resolved generation the index came from, never re-resolving current a second time -- the structural guarantee against a torn pair that section 7 states is the whole point of the generation-directory design.
criteria.verification: atlas/hookclient/tests/test_project_resolution.py: reads an index, then (simulating a concurrent republish between calls) changes what current points to, then calls read_project() using the FIRST read's result; asserts it reads the shard from the original resolved generation directory, not the new one current now points to.

criteria.statement: This component imports nothing outside the Python 3 standard library -- section 4's explicit 'zero dependencies' requirement for hookclient specifically (stricter than every other component's own 'no third-party dependencies' constraint, which still allows importing from elsewhere in this same project; hookclient may not even import atlas.resolve directly for this reason -- see out_of_scope).
criteria.verification: atlas/hookclient/tests/test_zero_deps.py: parses this component's own source files' import statements (ast module) and asserts every imported top-level module name is in the stdlib module list, with no import of any other atlas.* component.

failure_criteria.statement: A failure mode this component cannot fully classify falls through to a generic exception instead of a named reason, or worse, returns ok=True with partial/garbage data.
failure_criteria.detection: Every filesystem/parse operation in the read path is wrapped so its specific failure produces a named reason string; a catch-all handler at the top of the public function converts any OTHER unexpected exception into a named 'unexpected-error' reason rather than letting it propagate, so the 'never raises' guarantee holds even for a failure mode not in the original five.

failure_criteria.statement: A failure-mode count or timing number in this component's code comments or commit messages has no reproduction path.
failure_criteria.detection: grep the component's source and commit messages for numeric claims; each must name the command or test that produced it.

failure_criteria.statement: resolve_project assumes index['roots'] is well-formed (all string keys, all list-of-string prefixes) without defending against a corrupt or unexpected shape.
failure_criteria.detection: A fixture with a malformed roots entry (wrong type) is asserted to produce a named failure reason, not an unhandled exception.

failure_criteria.statement: A failure is written to a channel nobody reads (stderr print, a swallowed exception) instead of being returned in the result object.
failure_criteria.detection: Every failure path returns its reason in the result object's own field, which every test asserts on directly -- never a side-channel print.

out_of_scope: Importing atlas.resolve.matcher directly, despite C5 calling for the 'same matching logic' -- hookclient's zero-dependency constraint (C7) means it cannot import another atlas.* component (which itself is not zero-dependency-guaranteed transitively). This component vendors the same matching ALGORITHM as a small, independently-tested pure function, verified to produce identical output to atlas.resolve.matcher on the same fixtures (C5's verification), not a shared import.

Actually writing the fail-open fallback behavior inside a real Foreman hook -- this component is the read-side library a hook WOULD import; wiring it into architecture_gate.py or any other real hook is that hook's own future change, not this component's.
The severity rubric's actual content (still absent per FORE-32) -- reading severity_rubric.status='absent' correctly is in scope; interpreting a present rubric is not, since none exists yet.
Real end-to-end reads against a live-published snapshot directory -- this component's tests use synthetic fixtures; end-to-end correctness is foreman:integration-test's job.
constraints: Zero dependencies, stdlib only, and specifically no import of any other atlas.* module -- section 4's explicit requirement for this component, stricter than every sibling component's own constraint (C7).
No writes, no network, no subprocess -- read-only filesystem access exclusively.

Tests use Python's stdlib unittest, matching every other component's own convention (test code itself MAY import atlas.resolve.matcher for cross-checking in C5 -- the zero-dependency constraint applies to the shipped library, not its test suite).
